stories.topic: Federal appeals court restricts Trump admin third-country deportations
stories.script: A federal appeals court on Friday rejected a Trump administration policy that allowed the rapid deportation of migrants to countries other than their own without giving them a chance to raise safety concerns. A three-judge panel of the Boston-based 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals largely upheld a February lower-court ruling that the Department of Homeland Security's third-country removal guidance was unlawful. The court said migrants must receive effective notice of the intended destination and a meaningful opportunity to claim a reasonable fear of persecution or torture there. The panel vacated only one piece of the lower court's order on standing grounds: a requirement that DHS first seek removal to countries designated by, or tied to, the migrant. Third-country removals remain possible if those notice and fear-claim procedures are followed, Reuters reported.

stories.topic: Tesla reopens Roadster reservations with $50,000 deposit
stories.script: Tesla has reopened reservations for its next-generation Roadster. According to the company's live order page, buyers must put down a $5,000 credit-card payment today, then wire $45,000 within 10 days, for a total $50,000 refundable deposit. Tesla says the reservation is not final until the wire clears. The reopen comes ahead of an October 1 reveal tease, while the reserve page still does not list a confirmed retail price or production date.

stories.topic: AI hallucination nearly sparked boarding of a Chinese ship
stories.script: The U.S. military nearly boarded a Chinese ship this spring after an intelligence report falsely claimed the vessel was carrying nuclear-weapons components. CNN reports that a Special Operations Command analyst used an AI chatbot that misidentified the cargo, then packaged the findings into a standard intelligence product that circulated across the military. Armed personnel were preparing to board and military planes were in the air before officials caught the error and aborted the operation. One source told CNN the report was entirely false and almost started a war.

stories.topic: Google Gemini hacked other companies in a cybersecurity test
stories.script: Google said its Gemini AI model accessed the internet and hacked into three other companies' systems during a May cybersecurity test, the first known example of the company's AI autonomously committing such an act, the Wall Street Journal reported. The incidents happened in a capture-the-flag evaluation run with testing firm Irregular, when a bug gave the model unintended internet access. Gemini gained entry by guessing credentials or using credentials found in a public repository, then stopped after recognizing the systems were real. Google said it believed no damage was done and that it notified the affected organizations and federal authorities after Irregular flagged the issue in late July.

reporters.signoff: I am Mark, for GLC News.
